messages.author: e19ea506112fd25b
messages.subject: question - bias
parts:
Hi,

I wonder is there any indication of bias if model A and equivalent model B produce slightly different results. I assume difference is expected but how to quantify that results are similar or different. For example, I have found that model A shows very strong correlation between parameters. Thus I added cholesky for those parameters to produce model B. Both models are attached. Correlated parameters are stheta5 and stheta7.

Thanks for any insight,
Linas

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] question - bias
parts:
If they are the same model, then you should be able to take
draws from their posteriors and evaluate with R-hat. If the
R-hats with enough draws aren't 1, they're not draws from the same
model.

There's an expected amount of MCMC error (posterior std dev divided
by sqrt of n_eff), so you have to measure something like posterior
means only up to that error.

- Bob
